summary:
CaptionIQ v3 caption template & rendering engine — bug-fix retest run on the live preview URL as creator1@test.com. PRIMARY BUG 1 (caption covered whole video) is FIXED: overlay renders exactly 4 spans out of 12 total transcript words, and the caption

covers only ~5.2% of the video's pixel area. PRIMARY BUG 2 (chips only changed the font) is FIXED: 8 templates produced 8 distinct computed fontFamily values AND each carries a distinct colour/background — News shows a red box (rgb(220,38,38)), Modern's active word has an orange bg (rgb(250,93,41)) with white text, Gaming's active word has a purple bg (rgb(124,58,237)), Hype's active word is yellow (rgb(255,221,0)), etc. First word is marked data-active=true while paused so the theme is visible immediately, active-span count=1 across all templates. No /transcribe POST is issued when switching chips (0 during 8 chip clicks), and the transcript-panel caption-word list is byte-identical before and after switching. Style controls (position top/center/bottom, size S/M/L, uppercase toggle, box toggle) all mutate the renderer as expected. Playback advances the active word across 10 distinct words. Regression: transcript panel keeps its full semantic view (12 caption-word elements with entity coloring), logout redirects to /login. ONE NEW BUG FOUND: template persistence via localStorage is broken. Clicking template-chip-shorts writes {templateId:'shorts',...} to captioniq:style:, but after page reload the value is clobbered back to 'modern' and the Modern chip regains the active ring. Root cause is a classic effect-order race in Studio.jsx amplified by React.StrictMode: on the very first render (templateId defaults to 'modern' from useState), the load-effect runs first and calls setTemplateId('shorts'), but the save-effect immediately after runs with the STILL-STALE 'modern' closure value and overwrites localStorage. StrictMode then re-mounts, at which point the second load-effect reads back the just-clobbered 'modern' and no restore happens. Video: transcribe end-to-end still works (12 words with entities from real Whisper + gpt-5.4).
ai_feature_verdicts: Whisper transcription (POST /api/projects/{id}/transcribe) - pass - evidence: uploaded /app/test_fixtures/speech.mp3, waited 4s, transcript panel populated with 12 caption-word elements and the CaptionRenderer overlay populated with 4-word chunk 'Rahul went to Mumbai'. Only 1 network POST to /transcribe was observed (during the initial Generate click); 0 POSTs to /transcribe during 8 subsequent template-chip clicks. - skill: ai-testing-audio

gpt-5.4 entity tagging - pass - evidence: transcript panel keeps yellow(person)/blue(location)/green(action) entity coloring on Rahul/Priya/Mumbai/Delhi/went/shot after every chip switch (verified via caption-word[data-entity] survival). - skill: ai-testing-llm

Caption Template Engine (this iteration's UI focus, 11 client-side templates) - pass with 1 bug - evidence: 8 templates produced 8 distinct fontFamily + distinct active/box color signatures; ~4-word chunk rule works (renderer spans=4 vs 12 total words, caption/video area ratio=0.052); switching does NOT re-hit /transcribe; but localStorage persistence across reload is broken (see backend_issues.critical below — it is a frontend bug, tracked there for visibility). - skill: n/a (pure client-side rendering)

ui_bugs.issue: Selecting a template (e.g. Shorts) and reloading the studio page reverts to Modern. localStorage captioniq:style:<projectId> gets clobbered back to {templateId:'modern',...} during mount. RCA: two useEffects race — the load-effect setTemplateId('shorts') queues state, then the save-effect in the SAME commit runs with the still-stale closure value 'modern' and writes it to localStorage; React.StrictMode's second mount then reads that clobbered value. Suggested fix: initialise state lazily from localStorage inside useState() so no save happens before load, e.g. `useState(() => JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY))?.templateId || DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_ID)` — same pattern for settings — and remove the separate load-effect. Alternative: gate the save-effect behind a `hasLoadedRef.current` boolean that flips true only after the load-effect finishes.

action_items: Fix template persistence in frontend/src/pages/Studio.jsx: replace the load-effect with a lazy useState initialiser (or add a hasLoadedRef gate to the save-effect) so React.StrictMode's double-mount + first-render save can't clobber a previously-saved template.
Consider persisting the selected template on the backend project record too, so the user's choice survives switching browsers (currently client-only).
critical_code_review_comments: Studio.jsx has two coupled useEffects (load LS -> save LS) that race on mount and are especially broken under React.StrictMode. The canonical fix is a lazy initialiser in useState so the load is synchronous before any save can fire.
CaptionRenderer.jsx applies uniform per-word padding for layout stability — nice touch, prevents siblings from jittering when active word scales up. Verified spans do not shift during playback.

buildChunks in Studio.jsx uses fixed maxWords=4/maxGap=0.7s/maxDur=2.4s — this is what fixed BUG 1 by capping overlay length independent of Whisper segment size. It works on the test fixture (12 words -> 3 chunks of 4). Consider exposing these as user settings later.

TemplateBar chip previews render a single 'Aa' glyph using each template's font+active-color; this correctly hints at colour differences on the picker itself. No accessibility labels though — chips currently rely on the visible template name below.
Preview marks first word active only while currentTime < 0.25s. When the video is paused mid-clip on a chunk boundary the active-word colour may briefly disappear — minor UX polish.
seed_data_creation: None new. Reused /app/test_fixtures/speech.mp3 (~37 KB); a fresh project was created during the run and the second run reused it.
context_for_next_testing_agent: PRIMARY BUGS 1 and 2 from the review request are fully fixed and verified with computed-style assertions. The only regression uncovered this iteration is the template-persistence race in Studio.jsx (see frontend_issues.ui_bugs). Playwright commands used: login via input[type=email/password], create project by clicking [data-testid=new-project-btn] and immediately set_input_files on the hidden input[type=file] inside the dialog (there is no name field), transcribe via [data-testid=transcribe-btn], then read data-testid=caption-renderer for computed styles and iterate through template-chip-<id>. To reproduce the persistence bug: open any project, click template-chip-shorts, wait 500ms (LS becomes shorts), page.reload(), LS reverts to modern within the first commit.
rca of the issue: In frontend/src/pages/Studio.jsx the state hook `useState(DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_ID)` initialises templateId to 'modern' on every mount. Two useEffects then run in order: (1) load-effect reads localStorage and, if a saved template exists (say 'shorts'), calls setTemplateId('shorts'). (2) save-effect immediately runs in the same commit and writes JSON.stringify({templateId, settings}) using the closure value templateId='modern' (the queued setTemplateId hasn't reflected yet), clobbering localStorage. React re-renders with templateId='shorts' and the save-effect re-fires to correct localStorage — but React.StrictMode (enabled in src/index.js) unmounts and remounts the component; the remount's load-effect now reads the clobbered 'modern' from localStorage and setTemplateId('modern') stays. Net result: reload always resets to 'modern'. Fix: initialise state lazily from localStorage inside useState — e.g. `const [templateId, setTemplateId] = useState(() => { try { return JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY))?.templateId || DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_ID; } catch { return DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_ID; } });` and do the same for settings, then remove the load-effect entirely (only the save-effect remains). Or, keep the two effects but add `const hasLoadedRef = useRef(false)` and guard the save-effect with `if (!hasLoadedRef.current) return;` after the load-effect sets it true.
